items.q: A ball is kicked at 20. m/s at 30.° above the horizontal. What is the horizontal component of its velocity? (Degree mode.)

mistakes.why: Value: 10 m/s is v sin θ, the vertical component. The side next to the angle (horizontal here) uses cosine.
Value: your calculator is not in degree mode. Switch to degrees: cos 30° = 0.866.

why.correct: The horizontal side is adjacent to the angle: vₓ = v cos θ = (20. m/s)(cos 30°) = 17 m/s.

items.q: A hiker's displacement is 400 m at 53° north of east. What is the north component of the displacement? (Degree mode.)

mistakes.why: Value: 240 m is the east component, the side adjacent to the angle. North is opposite it: use sine.

why.correct: North is the side opposite the 53° angle (measured from east): d(north) = d sin θ = 400 m × sin 53° = 320 m (2 significant figures; 3.2 × 10² m).

items.q: A velocity has components vₓ = 9.0 m/s and v<sub>y</sub> = 12 m/s. What is its magnitude?

mistakes.why: Value: 21 m/s adds the components as if they pointed the same way. Perpendicular components combine with the Pythagorean theorem.

why.correct: The components are the legs of a right triangle and the velocity is the hypotenuse: v = √(9.0² + 12²) = √225 = 15 m/s.

items.q: A vector of magnitude A makes an angle θ with the vertical (y) axis. Which expression gives its horizontal (x) component?
options: A cos θ
A tan θ
A sin θ
A / cos θ

why.correct: Do not memorize "x uses cosine". Find the side adjacent to the angle you are given: it gets cosine; the opposite side gets sine.
options: Cosine gives the side adjacent to θ, which here is the vertical side.
Tangent is a ratio of the two legs, not a leg divided by the hypotenuse.
Right: measured from the vertical, the horizontal side is opposite θ, so it uses sine.
A component is shorter than the vector; dividing by cos θ makes it longer.

items.q: A student computes cos 60 on her calculator and gets −0.952. What went wrong?
options: Cosine of 60° is negative
The calculator is not in degree mode
She should have used sine
She should type the angle as 0.60

why.correct: Physics 1 angles are in degrees. Set the calculator to degree mode before any trig: cos 60° = 0.500.
options: Cosine is positive for angles from 0° to 90°.
Right: it read 60 in another angle unit and gave −0.952. In degree mode, cos 60° = 0.500.
Changing the function does not fix a calculator in the wrong angle mode.
Angles in degrees are entered as written; the mode is the problem.

items.q: A velocity has components vₓ = 12 m/s and v<sub>y</sub> = 5.0 m/s. What angle does it make above the horizontal, in degrees?

mistakes.why: Value: 67° is the angle from the vertical. Above the horizontal, the opposite side is v<sub>y</sub>: tan θ = v<sub>y</sub>/vₓ.
Value: that number is not in degrees. Set the calculator to degree mode and take tan⁻¹ again.

why.correct: tan θ = opposite/adjacent = v<sub>y</sub>/vₓ = 5.0/12, so θ = tan⁻¹(0.417) = 23°.

items.q: Two displacements are added tip to tail: 3.0 m east, then 4.0 m north. Which describes the total displacement?
options: 7.0 m, north of east
1.0 m, north
5.0 m, due north
5.0 m, north of east

why.correct: Tip to tail: draw the second vector starting at the tip of the first; the resultant goes from the first tail to the last tip. Here it is a 3-4-5 triangle.
options: Perpendicular displacements do not add as plain numbers; 7.0 m is the distance walked.
Subtracting works only for vectors along the same line in opposite directions.
The resultant points from the start to the end, which is north of east, not due north.
Right: the two legs are perpendicular, so the resultant is the hypotenuse √(3.0² + 4.0²) = 5.0 m, pointing between east and north.

items.q: A plane flies 240. km at 37.0° south of west, then 100. km due south. How far south of its start does it end? (Degree mode.)

mistakes.why: Value: you used the west component of leg 1. South is opposite the 37° angle measured from west: use sine.
Value: 340 km adds the whole first leg. Only its south component, 240 sin 37.0°, points south.

why.correct: Add the south components: leg 1 gives 240 km × sin 37.0° = 144.4 km south; leg 2 gives 100. km south. Total = 244 km.

items.q: A ball is launched at speed v at an angle θ above the horizontal. If the angle is increased (below 90°) at the same speed, what happens to the components?
options: Both components increase
The vertical component increases and the horizontal one decreases
The horizontal component increases and the vertical one decreases
Neither changes, because the speed is the same

why.correct: vₓ = v cos θ and v<sub>y</sub> = v sin θ. As θ rises, sin θ rises and cos θ falls; vₓ² + v<sub>y</sub>² stays v².
options: The magnitude is fixed, so one component can grow only if the other shrinks.
Right: v sin θ grows and v cos θ shrinks as θ increases toward 90°.
That happens when the angle decreases toward 0°.
The speed fixes the hypotenuse, but the angle decides how it splits between the legs.

items.q: A 3.0 m ramp makes an angle of 25° with the floor. How high is the top of the ramp above the floor? (Degree mode.)

mistakes.why: Value: 2.7 m is the horizontal length of the ramp, adjacent to the angle. The height is opposite: use sine.

why.correct: The ramp is the hypotenuse; its height is the side opposite the 25° angle: h = (3.0 m) sin 25° = 1.3 m.

items.q: In a right triangle, which ratio is cos θ?
options: opposite / hypotenuse
opposite / adjacent
hypotenuse / adjacent
adjacent / hypotenuse

why.correct: CAH: cosine is adjacent over hypotenuse, where the adjacent side is the leg that touches the angle θ.
options: That is sin θ (SOH).
That is tan θ (TOA).
That is upside down. The hypotenuse is the longest side, so this ratio would be more than 1, and a cosine never is.
Right: the leg touching the angle, divided by the longest side.

items.q: A student splits a 20. m/s velocity into components and reports a horizontal component of 26 m/s. Without redoing the work, how do you know this is wrong?
options: A horizontal component must always be smaller than the vertical one
A component cannot be larger than the vector it comes from
A component must be exactly half of the vector
Components of a velocity cannot be given in m/s

why.correct: The vector is the hypotenuse of the right triangle, and the components are its legs. A leg is never longer than the hypotenuse, so no component can be more than 20. m/s.
options: Either component can be the larger one. It depends on the angle.
Right: sine and cosine are never more than 1, so A cos θ and A sin θ are never more than A.
A component is half the vector only at special angles, such as cos 60°.
Components carry the same unit as the vector.

items.q: A ramp rises 1.5 m and makes an angle of 30.° with the floor. How long is the ramp (the sloping side)?

mistakes.why: Value: you multiplied by sin 30°. The rise is the opposite side, so rise = L sin θ and L = rise ÷ sin θ.
Value: you used cosine. The rise is opposite the 30° angle, so use sine.

why.correct: The rise is opposite the angle and the ramp is the hypotenuse: sin 30.° = 1.5 m / L, so L = 1.5 m ÷ 0.50 = 3.0 m.

items.q: Displacement A is 5.0 m east. Displacement B has components 3.0 m east and 4.0 m north. What are the components of the sum A + B?
options: 8.0 m east and 4.0 m north
5.0 m east and 5.0 m north
10. m east and 0 m north
3.0 m east and 9.0 m north

why.correct: Add the east parts and the north parts separately. East: 5.0 m + 3.0 m = 8.0 m. North: 0 + 4.0 m = 4.0 m.
options: Right: each direction is added on its own.
B has a magnitude of 5.0 m, but its magnitude is not a north component. Only its 4.0 m north part counts toward north.
That adds the two magnitudes, 5.0 m and 5.0 m, as if both pointed east.
A points east, so its 5.0 m belongs with the east parts, not the north parts.

items.q: For the 3-4-5 triangle, sin 37° ≈ 0.60. Without a calculator, what is cos 53°?
options: About 0.80
About 0.40
About 0.60
About 0.75

why.correct: 37° and 53° are the two smaller angles of the same right triangle. The side opposite 37° is the side adjacent to 53°, so sin 37° = cos 53° ≈ 0.60.
options: 0.80 is cos 37°, which equals sin 53°.
1 − 0.60 is not a trig rule. Use the triangle: the same side is opposite one angle and adjacent to the other.
Right: 3/5 either way.
0.75 is 3/4, which is tan 37°.

items.q: A displacement of 100 m points 10° above the +x-axis. Which pair of components is reasonable?
options: About 17 m along x and 98 m along y
About 50 m along x and 50 m along y
About 71 m along x and 71 m along y
About 98 m along x and 17 m along y

why.correct: A small angle from the x-axis means the vector lies almost along x: a big x-component and a small y-component. 100 cos 10° ≈ 98 m and 100 sin 10° ≈ 17 m.
options: These are swapped. The vector is close to the x-axis, so the x-component is the big one.
These do not rebuild the vector: √(50² + 50²) is about 71 m, not 100 m.
Equal components belong to a 45° angle.
Right: and √(98² + 17²) is about 100 m, so the components rebuild the vector.
